articles.title: Glandular Tissue Component at Preoperative Breast US and Recurrence Risk in Invasive Breast Cancer.
articles.abstract: Background Glandular tissue component (GTC) at breast US is associated with breast cancer risk, but recurrence risk remains unclear. Purpose To evaluate the association between GTC assessed at preoperative breast US and recurrence risk in invasive breast cancer across two tertiary institutions in Korea and China. Materials and Methods This retrospective longitudinal study included consecutive women with invasive breast cancer who underwent surgery between January 2013 and December 2018 in Korea and between January 2013 and December 2019 in China. GTC was qualitatively classified as low (minimal or mild) or high (moderate or marked) on preoperative bilateral US images. GTC was prospectively assessed during routine clinical care at institution A (Korea) and retrospectively assessed using archived images at institution B (China). Competing-risk multivariable Fine-Gray models evaluated GTC as the independent variable for recurrence, with adjustment for clinicopathologic variables. Results Mean age was 52.4 years ± 10.8 (SD) at institution A (n = 5167) and 49.2 years ± 10.1 at institution B (n = 3719). Median interval from surgery to recurrence diagnosis or last follow-up was 6.8 years (IQR, 5.42-8.41 years) at institution A and 8.0 years (IQR, 6.38-9.60 years) at institution B. Ipsilateral or contralateral breast cancer occurred in 145 (2.8%) and 85 patients (2.3%) at institutions A and B, respectively, while regional or distant recurrence occurred in 233 (4.5%) and 520 (14.0%). In multivariable analyses, high GTC was independently associated with increased risk of ipsilateral or contralateral breast cancer at institution A (subdistribution hazard ratio [HR], 1.93; P < .001) and institution B (HR, 2.02; P = .002). There was no evidence of an association between GTC and regional or distant recurrence at either institution A (HR, 0.89; P = .46) or institution B (HR, 1.20; P = .06). Conclusion High GTC at preoperative breast US was independently associated with an increased risk of ipsilateral or contralateral breast cancer after invasive breast cancer treatment, consistently across both institutions. © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article.

articles.title: Racial and Ethnic Disparities in Guideline-Concordant Breast Imaging Surveillance among BRCA1 and BRCA2 Variant Carriers.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate racial and ethnic differences in longitudinal, age-appropriate breast imaging surveillance among carriers of BRCA1/2 variants. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included females with pathogenic or likely pathogenic BRCA1/2 variants in the All of Us Research Program. Surveillance was evaluated at semiannual timepoints from 2016-2024 using rolling 12-month windows. Guideline-concordant surveillance was defined as breast MRI at ages 25-29 years and MRI and screening mammography at age 30 years or older. Generalized estimating equation models evaluated racial and ethnic associations in surveillance, adjusting for age, body mass index, Area Deprivation Index, calendar time, and electronic health record (EHR) activity. RESULTS: Among 6,125 participants, 3,221 (52.6%) were Hispanic, 2,321 (37.9%) non-Hispanic White, 300 (4.9%) non-Hispanic Black, and 283 (4.6%) Other/Multiracial. Compared with non-Hispanic White participants, Hispanic (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.14; 95% CI: 0.08-0.28) and Other/Multiracial participants (aOR, 0.37; 95% CI: 0.15-0.95) had lower odds of guideline-concordant surveillance. Hispanic participants had lower odds of MRI (aOR, 0.22; 95% CI: 0.13-0.37) and mammography (aOR, 0.67; 95% CI: 0.56-0.79); non-Hispanic Black participants had lower odds of mammography (aOR, 0.57; 95% CI: 0.36-0.91). Over time, the difference in the odds of screening mammography between Hispanic and non-Hispanic White participants widened (OR per year, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.91-0.99). CONCLUSION: Racial and ethnic differences in guideline-concordant breast imaging surveillance were observed among BRCA1/2 variant carriers, particularly among Hispanic participants, indicating persistent disparities in recommended surveillance within this high-risk population.

articles.title: ContextMRI: Enhancing compressed sensing MRI through metadata conditioning.
articles.abstract: Compressed sensing MRI seeks to accelerate MRI acquisition processes by sampling fewer k-space measurements and then reconstructing the missing data algorithmically. The success of these approaches often relies on strong priors or learned statistical models. While recent diffusion model-based priors have shown great potential, previous methods typically ignore clinically available metadata (e.g. patient demographics, imaging parameters, slice-specific information). In practice, metadata contains meaningful cues about the anatomy and acquisition protocol, suggesting it could further constrain the reconstruction problem. In this work, we propose ContextMRI, a text-conditioned diffusion model for MRI that integrates granular metadata into the reconstruction process. We train a pixel-space diffusion model directly on minimally processed, complex-valued MRI images. During inference, metadata is converted into a structured text prompt and fed to the model via CLIP text embeddings. By conditioning the prior on metadata, we unlock more accurate reconstructions and show consistent gains across multiple datasets, acceleration factors, and undersampling patterns. Our experiments demonstrate that increasing the fidelity of metadata - ranging from slice location and contrast to patient age, sex, and pathology - systematically boosts reconstruction performance. This work highlights the untapped potential of leveraging clinical context for inverse problems and opens a new direction for metadata-driven MRI reconstruction. Code is available at https://github.com/DoHunLee1/ContextMRI.

articles.title: Multi-phase liver CT virtual contrast enhancement and diagnosis based on phase-aware diffusion network.
articles.abstract: Multi-phase contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) plays a crucial role in liver tumor diagnosis but is limited by additional radiation exposure and a restricted patient population. While virtual contrast enhancement (VCE) methods can generate virtual liver CECT images, challenges persist due to detail-deficient non-contrast CT (NCCT) images and phase-wise feature variations. In this paper, we propose phase-aware diffusion (PA-Diff), a novel model for multi-phase liver CT enhancement and contrast-agent-free liver tumor diagnosis, which combines two novel designs: 1) Phase-specific path allocation that enables precise multi-phase enhancement by combining independent diffusion paths and shared encoder and decoder; 2) Cycle re-encoding learning that enhances tumor detail by recovering target images and re-encoding them into complementary features for loss calculation during training. We also perform automatic diagnosis on the VCE CT images. Experiments on two dataset demonstrate effective multi-phase enhancement and accurate Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC) screening and Microvascular Invasion (MVI) diagnosis, highlighting the model's clinical value.

articles.title: Multiparametric MRI to predict response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in breast cancer: Are we ready for NacBI-RADS?
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Accurate assessment of treatment response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) in breast cancer (BC) is crucial for guiding surgical planning. While size-based criteria remain standard, they may underestimate therapy-induced biological changes. To develop and validate the neoadjuvant breast imaging reporting and data system (NacBI-RADS), a structured multiparametric MRI (mp-MRI) lexicon was designed to evaluate NAC response and support surgical decision-making. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 68 BC patients who underwent staging and post-NAC MRI, followed by surgery. mp-MRI examinations included contrast-enhanced T1, T2-weighted, and diffusion-weighted imaging. NacBI-RADS integrates four parameters: peritumoral edema, ΔADC (apparent diffusion coefficient change), post-contrast tumor size, and lymph node status (Node-RADS). Three independent breast radiologists evaluated all cases. Inter-reader agreement was assessed with Cohen's and Fleiss' kappa. RESULTS: Of 88 patients assessed, 68 were included. Residual disease was found in 43 patients (63%) and pathological complete response in 25 (37%). Most lesions were categorized as NacBI-RADS 1-2, while categories 4-5 were less frequent (12-15%). NacBI-RADS showed high diagnostic performance (AUC 0.942-0.960) with excellent reproducibility (κ 0.931-0.953). Lower categories were associated with complete or near-complete response, and higher categories with residual disease (p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: This exploratory study suggests that NacBI-RADS may offer a standardized and reproducible mp-MRI framework for assessing NAC response. Further studies are needed to confirm its role in imaging-guided surgical planning. KEY POINTS: Question Can a structured mp-MRI framework improve the accuracy and reproducibility of assessing BC response to NAC compared with conventional size-based criteria? Findings NacBI-RADS showed high diagnostic accuracy (AUC up to 0.960) and excellent inter-reader agreement, reliably distinguishing complete/partial-complete responders from patients with residual disease. Clinical relevance NacBI-RADS may support more accurate and reproducible response assessment after NAC, helping identify true complete responders and aiding safe, personalized surgical de-escalation strategies in BC management.

articles.title: Comparison of 7-T and 3-T MRI for the Detection of Multiple Sclerosis Lesions.
articles.abstract: Background MRI is central to multiple sclerosis (MS) diagnosis. Although 7-T MRI improves lesion detection compared with 3-T MRI, systematic head-to-head comparisons across lesion locations and key imaging biomarkers, including the central vein sign (CVS) and paramagnetic rim lesions (PRLs), remain limited; consensus statements call for such studies to better define the clinical value of 7-T MRI. Purpose To systematically compare 7-T and 3-T MRI for detecting MS lesions across characteristic intracranial regions and key imaging biomarkers and to assess the incremental clinical value of 7-T MRI for lesion detection. Materials and Methods Patients with MS from the China National Registry of Neuro-Inflammatory Diseases were prospectively enrolled and underwent same-day 7-T and 3-T MRI examinations (March 2023 to June 2024). Images were anonymized and independently interpreted by two experienced raters in a blinded manner according to standard criteria. Lesion counts were compared with the Wilcoxon signed-rank test; inter- and intrarater reliability were assessed with the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) and Cohen κ, respectively. Results Among 30 participants (median age at MRI, 34.5 years [IQR, 30-48.3 years]; 27 female), 7-T MRI depicted more MS lesions overall than 3-T MRI (2268 vs 1779; relative increase, 27.5%; P < .001), with higher detection across cortical (+135.7%), juxtacortical (+26.1%), periventricular (+18.8%), and infratentorial (+33.5%) regions (all P < .001). Moreover, 7-T MRI visualized more CVS-positive lesions (1451 vs 592; +145.1%; P < .001) and more PRLs (634 vs 468; +35.5%; P < .001). The proportion of CVS-positive lesions was higher with 7-T MRI than with 3-T MRI (64.0% vs 33.3%, P < .001), whereas the proportions of PRLs were similar (28.0% vs 26.3%, P = .057). Interrater reliability was excellent (ICC = 0.99). Conclusion Compared with 3-T MRI, 7-T MRI improved MS lesion detection across characteristic intracranial regions and key imaging biomarkers, with a higher proportion of CVS-positive lesions but similar PRL proportions, supporting the clinical value of 7-T MRI. Low-Dose CT Lung-RADS 2022 for the Management of Screening- and Non-Screening-detected Lung Cancer Associated with Cystic Airspaces.
articles.abstract: Background Lung cancer associated with cystic airspaces (CA) can be misinterpreted as a benign lesion, leading to missed or delayed diagnosis; however, the effect of the Lung Imaging Reporting and Data System (Lung-RADS) 2022 criteria remains unverified. Purpose To retrospectively determine the frequency and outcomes of lung cancer associated with CA during screening and explore the potential effect of Lung-RADS 2022 on earlier diagnosis. Materials and Methods This secondary analysis included participants with lung cancers from three trials: the National Lung Screening Trial (2002-2007); Italian Lung Cancer Screening Trial, or ITALUNG (2004-2010); and German Lung Cancer Screening Intervention trial, or LUSI (2007-2016). Two radiologists jointly reviewed low-dose CT images to identify and morphologically characterize lung cancer associated with CA. Associations with histologic features, stage, and other variables were assessed. Lung cancer-specific survival was analyzed using Fine-Gray regression accounting for the competing risk of non-lung cancer death. Multivariable models were adjusted for age, sex, stage, detection status, and trial. Lung-RADS 2022 criteria for atypical pulmonary cysts were applied. Results Seventy-three cancers associated with CA were identified in 1258 participants (median age, 64 years [IQR, 61-69 years]; 43 male), including 44 of 716 (6.1%) screening-detected and 29 of 542 (5.4%) non-screening-detected cancers. Multilocular morphologic type was associated with a more advanced stage than unilocular morphologic type (12 of 24 vs 15 of 49; P = .02). The 5-year lung cancer-specific survival was 51.4% (95% CI: 39.3, 62.3) for cancers associated with CA and 53.2% (95% CI: 50.1, 56.2) for 1054 participants with noncystic non-small cell lung cancer. No evidence of a difference in survival was observed (subdistribution hazard ratio, 1.15 [95% CI: 0.81, 1.63]; P = .44), and results remained consistent in multivariable models. Lung-RADS 2022 might have enabled earlier diagnosis in 55 of 73 cancers associated with CA (75%). Conclusion Lung cancer associated with CA accounted for 6.1% of screening-detected and 5.4% of non-screening-detected lung cancers. Outcomes were similar to those of noncystic non-small cell lung cancer, and Lung-RADS 2022 may facilitate earlier diagnosis. Clinical trial registration nos. NCT00047385, NCT02777996, and ISRCTN N30604390 © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article. See also the editorial by Byrne and Hammer in this issue.

articles.title: Gadolinium Retention in Pediatric Bone: Linear versus Macrocyclic MRI Contrast Agents.
articles.abstract: Background Gadolinium retention in bone after gadolinium-based contrast agent (GBCA) exposure is documented in adults but unquantified in children, who may have higher cumulative doses from early imaging. Purpose To quantify and compare residual gadolinium in pediatric bone tissue after macrocyclic and linear GBCA exposure. Materials and Methods In this prospective pilot study, individuals under 18 years of age scheduled for median sternotomy who had undergone clinically indicated GBCA-enhanced or unenhanced MRI were included between January 2018 and August 2024 at a single academic medical center and categorized into three groups: linear GBCA exposed (gadobenate), macrocyclic GBCA exposed (gadoterate), and control (no GBCA exposure). Bone samples were obtained during surgery and analyzed for gadolinium concentration (micrograms of gadolinium per gram of bone tissue). Linear regression modeling was used to analyze the impact of GBCA exposure on bone gadolinium concentration. Results A total of 29 individuals were included: nine exposed to linear GBCA (median age, 12.0 years [IQR, 4.0-14.0 years]; five male individuals), 11 exposed to macrocyclic GBCA (median age, 13.0 years [IQR, 3.3-14.8 years]; eight male individuals), and nine control individuals (median age, 1.8 years [IQR, 0.5-6.3 years]; seven male individuals). Gadolinium was detected in bone tissue in all groups. Median bone gadolinium concentrations were 0.001 μg/g (IQR, 0.0007-0.0015 μg/g) with no GBCA exposure, 0.007 μg/g (IQR, 0.004-0.011 μg/g) with gadoterate exposure, and 0.141 μg/g (IQR, 0.079-0.374 μg/g) with gadobenate exposure. GBCA exposure was associated with gadolinium concentration (adjusted R2 = 0.77; P < .001). Gadobenate exposure was associated with higher gadolinium concentrations than no GBCA exposure (lnβ [log-transformed regression coefficient] = 4.9 [95% CI: 3.7, 5.9]; fold change, 129.8; P < .001) and gadoterate exposure (lnβ = 2.8 [95% CI: 1.6, 3.8]; fold change, 16.0; P < .001). Gadoterate exposure was also associated with higher gadolinium concentrations than no GBCA exposure (lnβ = 2.1 [95% CI: 1.5, 2.7]; fold change, 8.1; P < .001). Conclusion Exposure to the linear agent gadobenate at MRI was associated with higher gadolinium concentrations in bone tissue than no GBCA exposure or exposure to the macrocyclic agent gadoterate; trace gadolinium in the bone tissue of controls may reflect environmental exposure. Recent advances in photoacoustic imaging for breast reconstruction using the abdominal flap.
articles.abstract: Recent advances in diagnostic imaging have significantly impacted surgical planning and options. In breast reconstruction using abdominal flaps, a method employing flaps from the lower abdomen allows for a high-quality reconstruction with a morphology and texture resembling those of the contralateral breast. Understanding microvascular patterns is crucial in this surgery to prevent volume deficiencies and contribute to successful tissue transplantation while maintaining the softness of the tissue. While the location and number of "perforators"-arteriovenous bundles penetrating the anterior sheath of the rectus abdominis-have traditionally been the focus, recent studies have further emphasized the importance of selecting appropriate perforating vessels to maintain the vascular network within the superficial adipose tissue and subcutaneous tissue and to elevate a high-quality flap with extensive and stable blood flow. Clinical studies using contrast-enhanced CT have drawn attention to the midline-crossing arterial network, demonstrating its relationship with a wide range of hemodynamic areas. Preoperatively, clearly identifying the blood vessels linking the left and right sides of the abdominal midline provides valuable information for planning free DIEP flaps for breast reconstruction, ensuring stable blood flow to the flap. However, clear visualization with contrast-enhanced CT requires high volumes of contrast agents, and color Doppler ultrasound has difficulty visualizing horizontally; therefore, a non-invasive and superior imaging method is required. Photoacoustic imaging can comprehensively and noninvasively visualize the subcutaneous vascular network and is attracting attention as a new preoperative examination technique. We conducted clinical research using newly developed medical photoacoustic imaging and reported the results and future challenges in several publications. We have also recently reported the impact of abdominal surgical scars on the midline-crossing artery. This review summarizes the current trends in preoperative vascular studies for breast reconstruction using abdominal flaps and discusses the current state of evolving photoacoustic imaging technology.

Spontaneously emerging patterns show category-biased similarity to task-evoked visual patterns beyond human visual cortex.
articles.abstract: In the absence of any task, spontaneous brain activity exhibits patterns that resemble those evoked by natural stimuli and behaviors. This raises the possibility that resting-state activity patterns may relate to maintenance and consolidation of behaviorally relevant information states. Using functional MRI (fMRI) data from 100 healthy adults in the Human Connectome Project, we investigated whether neural signals evoked by specific visual stimuli (body parts, faces, places, tools) show similarity to resting-state activity across non-canonical visual areas, i.e., motor and association cortices. Participants underwent a working memory task and resting-state scanning. We analyzed multivoxel pattern similarity between task-evoked activations and spontaneous activity in bilateral hand motor regions and attention-related networks. Spatial correlations between task-evoked multivoxel patterns for each visual category and frame-by-frame resting-state signals were computed, with the upper 90% distribution percentile (U90) as a similarity metric. We found that resting-state patterns in the left hemisphere hand motor region showed significantly higher similarity to tool-evoked patterns than place-evoked patterns, consistent with the interpretation that tools recruit motor affordances and hand‑object associations in motor cortex. In the bilateral dorsal attention network, resting-task similarity for non-face evoked patterns significantly exceeded that for faces. Moreover, effects localized to posterior dorsal attention network, aligning with the dorsal visual pathway's role in spatial-action coding of behaviorally relevant objects. These results suggest that resting-state activity in non-visual cortices shows category-biased similarity to task-evoked visual patterns, consistent with the view that spontaneous neural dynamics preferentially reactivate ecologically salient stimuli.

articles.title: Do S-Detect and ChatGPT Improve Diagnostic Performance and Agreement with BI-RADS Morphologic Descriptors Among Early-career Radiologists?
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: We investigated whether S-Detect and ChatGPT assistance improve early-career radiologists' diagnostic performance in breast ultrasound and their agreement with a senior breast radiologist (SBR) for Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System v5.0 morphologic descriptors. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Ultrasound images of 299 histopathologically confirmed lesions from 268 patients were retrospectively evaluated by the SBR, one junior attending radiologist, three residents, S-Detect, and ChatGPT (single image-only zero-shot inference via the web interface). These four early-career radiologists reassessed lesions with S-Detect and ChatGPT assistance. Histopathology was the reference standard for diagnostic performance, and the SBR for descriptor agreement. Kappa differences were compared using patient-level cluster bootstrapping. RESULTS: The SBR achieved the highest sensitivity and accuracy, whereas S-Detect achieved the highest specificity. Neither S-Detect nor ChatGPT assistance consistently improved diagnostic performance. S-Detect had the highest standalone agreement for shape, margin, posterior acoustic features, and echo pattern, and S-Detect assistance significantly improved agreement for shape, posterior acoustic features, and echo pattern in selected readers. Histopathologic agreement was highest for the SBR (κ = 0.713; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.637-0.789), followed by S-Detect (κ = 0.686; 95% CI, 0.604-0.768), without significant difference (difference in kappa, -0.027; 95% CI, -0.128-0.067; Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted q = 0.877); however, the wide CI could not exclude a clinically meaningful difference. ChatGPT had the lowest agreement (κ = 0.373; 95% CI, 0.271-0.474). CONCLUSION: In this biopsy-confirmed cohort, S-Detect showed high specificity and strong descriptor agreement but did not consistently enhance early-career radiologists' diagnostic performance. ChatGPT performance was limited under image-only, single-inference zero-shot conditions and should not be generalized to its overall capability.

articles.title: Low-Dose PCCT-Based Liver Volume Perfusion CT with Phase-Specific Reconstruction Optimization for Morphologic.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Volume perfusion CT (VPCT) of the liver provides functional information but is associated with increased radiation exposure and often requires additional multiphasic CT acquisitions. Photon-counting CT (PCCT) may enable low-dose one-stop imaging by generating diagnostic morphological images directly from perfusion datasets. To evaluate the image quality of single-phase and fused noncontrast and contrast-enhanced images generated from photon-counting CT (PCCT)-based liver dynamic volume perfusion CT (VPCT) for liver morphologic assessment. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this prospective study, 62 patients with liver disease underwent true noncontrast PCCT, liver VPCT, and low-dose delayed-phase imaging. Single-time-point noncontrast, arterial-phase, and portal venous-phase images were reconstructed from the VPCT dataset using virtual monoenergetic image (VMI, 40-70 keV) and Threshold 3D (T3D) reconstruction. Fused T3D images were generated from multiphase perfusion data. Image quality was evaluated using signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), subjective image-quality scores. Radiation dose was recorded. RESULTS: The one-stop imaging protocol yielded a lower effective dose than the simulated conventional four-phase protocol combined with perfusion imaging (25.9 ± 6.7 mSv vs 31.9 ± 8.5 mSv, P < 0.05). Compared with true noncontrast images, fused noncontrast images showed higher SNR (8.6 ± 3.0 vs 7.0 ± 1.9) and CNR (1.5 ± 1.2 vs 1.0 ± 0.8) (P < 0.05). Although subjective image-quality scores for perfusion-derived noncontrast images were lower than those for true noncontrast images, all remained diagnostically acceptable (score ≥ 3). In the arterial phase, fused images showed the lowest image noise (7.5 ± 2.7 HU), while 40-keV VMI provided the highest CNR (70.4 ± 24.0). In the portal venous phase, fused images achieved the lowest noise (8.8 ± 2.8 HU) while maintaining relatively high CNR (10.4 ± 7.8). Except for 40-keV and 50-keV portal venous-phase images, all reconstructed arterial- and portal venous-phase images achieved diagnostically acceptable subjective scores (≥3). CONCLUSION: PCCT-based liver VPCT one-stop imaging reduces radiation exposure while providing diagnostically acceptable morphologic images. The optimal reconstruction of noncontrast and contrast-enhanced images varies by imaging phase, supporting a phase-specific image optimization strategy for liver morphologic assessment.

articles.title: A Multichannel and Multimodal Combined Model Based on 2.5D Deep Learning For Predicting Tumor-Free Survival After Liver Transplantation In Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A 7-Year Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) accounts for 90% of primary liver cancers and ranks as the fourth leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide. This study aimed to promptly identify high-risk patients for early recurrence after liver transplantation (LT), thereby optimizing personalized follow-up and intervention strategies for patients with HCC. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective cohort of 143 patients with HCC was selected. Following the collection of imaging investigations, clinical data, and postoperative follow-up information, we developed a combined model based on 2.5-dimensional (2.5D) deep learning (DL). This model integrates clinical features, radiomics characteristics, and DL data across multiple modalities, utilizing multichannel 2.5D data comprising coronal, sagittal, and peritumoral slices of the largest tumor area. Model performance was assessed through receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). RESULTS: The 2.5D DL model demonstrated superior performance over the 2D DL model, achieving area under the ROC curve (AUC) values of 0.784/0.842, 0.799/0.843, and 0.824/0.827 in the training and testing cohorts, compared to the 2D model's 0.736/0.819, 0.751/0.818, and 0.724/0.803. The combined model significantly surpassed other models, attaining C-index values of 0.789/0.826 in the training and testing cohorts, along with 1-year, 2-year, and 3-year AUC values of 0.842/0.931, 0.865/0.891, and 0.853/0.885, respectively. Furthermore, the combined model demonstrated the highest consistency in calibration curves and provided the greatest clinical net benefit in DCA. CONCLUSION: The combined model based on 2.5D DL demonstrates robust applicability and high predictive performance in identifying early postoperative recurrence of HCC. This strategy facilitates proactive and individualized intervention for high-risk patients, thereby improving clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Age- and Sex-Specific Reference Curves of Posterior Cranial Fossa Structures in Children: The BIOMAP-PCF Study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: The posterior cranial fossa (PCF) houses structures that are critical for neurological development and the integrated functioning of the central nervous system. Despite their clinical relevance, age and sex-specific reference biometric data in pediatrics remain limited. Aim of this study was to perform a Biometric Investigation Of Morphology and Anatomy in the Pediatric PCF (BIOMAP-PCF), to provide age- and sex-specific reference curves of these structures in a large pediatric population. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective two-center study, 3D T1-weighted images of 1054 pediatric subjects from 0 to 18 years were analyzed (9.0±5.0 years, M/F=508/546). Different linear and cross-sectional area measurements of PCF structures were obtained, and age- and sex-specific reference intervals for each variable were estimated using the Royston and Wright method. To better evaluate the pattern of age-dependent changes between posterior cranial fossa structures, selected ratios were calculated. RESULTS: Reference values (3rd, median and 97th percentile) were obtained for each parameter. All measures showed nonlinear growth, with rapid changes in early childhood followed by progressive slowing. Ratios showed stable anteroposterior brainstem proportions across age, while the pons-to-midbrain craniocaudal ratio showed a mild age-related increase. Intra- and interobserver agreement was excellent (ICC>0.90) for all parameters, with the only exception of one measure showing an ICC=0.89. CONCLUSIONS: We provide highly reproducible age- and sex-specific reference curves for PCF structures in pediatric populations. Linear and cross-sectional area measurements, together with brainstem ratios, provide a reproducible, clinically applicable framework for quantitative assessment of PCF development in children.

articles.title: Comparative Analysis of Visual Emphysema Detection with Low Attenuation Area Quantification: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To systematically review CT-based LAA% for emphysema quantification, explore the application of percentage low attenuation area (LAA% below -950HU), in comparison with visual emphysema scoring. METHODS: Following PRISMA-DTA guidelines, searches were conducted (01-01-1972 to 01-04-2026) in PubMed, Embase®, and Web of Science databases to identify English-language studies of adults ≥18 years with CT-quantified emphysema. Two independent readers screened titles, abstracts and full texts against predefined inclusion/exclusion criteria. Studies comparing LAA%-quantified emphysema with visual scores were included. RESULTS: 737 studies were reviewed, 5 (0.7%) met the eligibility criteria. These studies originated from Asia, Europe and the United States. LAA% cut-off values for emphysema varied: two studies used a 6% threshold, one used 5%, another used 1.5%, and one applied ordinal severity thresholds from 1% to 25%. Visual classification also differed, with three studies using the Fleischner Society system, one using a modified 3-point score, and another using the Goddard classification. Agreement between visual assessment and LAA%-based quantification was generally poor, with reported kappa values of 0.22 (n = 1,221), -0.06 (n = 200), and 0.48 (n = 98). Two studies further reported agreement based on sensitivity (86.8% and 58.0%) and specificity (84.2% and 39.0%). CONCLUSIONS: Based on limited evidence, substantial heterogeneity exists between visual assessment and LAA% quantification in emphysema. Discordance between visual and quantitative CT assessment likely reflects differences in diagnostic criteria and technical characteristics, highlighting the need for standardized reporting and methodology. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This systematic review provides a comprehensive comparison of visual scoring and LAA% metrics. It demonstrates limited agreement and substantial methodological heterogeneity of CT assessment of emphysema.

articles.title: Neural Connectome Mapping of Chronotype in Young Adults: Associations with Neurotransmitter Profiles and Longitudinal Self-Control.
articles.abstract: Chronotype is associated with self-regulation, but its functional connectivity correlates, neurotransmitter correspondence, and longitudinal associations with self-control remain unclear. We applied connectome-based predictive modeling (CPM) in a longitudinal cohort to identify resting-state connectivity features associated with chronotype. Cross-validated predictions showed a small correlation with reduced Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire (rMEQ) scores in the discovery set (n = 816, r = 0.118, pperm = 0.007). A similar association was observed in validation set 1, a baseline hold-out sample from the same cohort (n = 681, r = 0.125, pperm < 0.001). Longitudinal evaluation used validation set 2, comprising two-year follow-up data from a subset of participants in validation set 1 (n = 594, r = 0.134, pperm < 0.001), providing a within-cohort assessment of whether the association was stable over time. Node-importance maps showed spatial correspondence with neurotransmitter maps. Both connectivity sets shared GABA-A and VAChT associations, with relatively receptor-weighted and transporter-weighted profiles in the positive and negative sets, respectively. In participants with complete two-wave data (n = 563), cross-lagged panel models indicated that baseline self-control was prospectively associated with higher positive-set strength (β = 0.256, p < 0.001) and lower negative-set strength (β = -0.228, p < 0.001); reverse paths were not significant. These findings provide evidence for chronotype-related functional connectivity features and their associations with neurotransmitter distributions and self-control in young adults. The validation and longitudinal evidence is limited to a single-site cohort, and cross-cohort generalizability remains to be established.

articles.title: Static and dynamic intrinsic brain activity in eyes-closed and eyes-open resting-state conditions.
articles.abstract: Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging data are typically acquired under eyes-closed (EC) or eyes-open (EO) conditions, which are thought to reflect interoceptive and exteroceptive brain states. However, evidence for condition-dependent differences has largely relied on static analyses that provide limited information about temporal variability. Here, we investigated eye-state modulation of intrinsic brain activity by integrating multimetric static and dynamic analyses across multiple spatial scales. Static measures, including the amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations (ALFF), fractional ALFF (fALFF), regional homogeneity (ReHo), and degree centrality (DC), were estimated to characterize low-frequency amplitude, relative spectral contribution, local synchronization, and network centrality. A sliding-window approach was used to calculate ALFF, fALFF, ReHo, and DC within successive windows, and their variability across windows was quantified. Static analyses revealed spatial differences between EC and EO across visual, sensorimotor, temporal, prefrontal, parietal, and subcortical regions. A particularly consistent finding across the static metrics was greater middle occipital gyrus involvement during EO. However, fALFF also showed an EC-related increase in the left calcarine cortex, indicating regionally heterogeneous effects within the occipital cortex. Dynamic analyses showed greater variability during EC in selected posterior visual regions, most consistently for dALFF and dReHo variability, whereas dfALFF and dDC variability were more sensitive to window length, mean adjustment, and spatial standardization. These findings demonstrate that eye state modulates intrinsic brain function through coordinated changes in both whole-scan measures and temporal variability across multiple spatial scales, highlighting the importance of jointly considering static and dynamic properties when investigating the neural organization of resting-state activity.

articles.title: Audio large language models align with human neural responses during spoken-language comprehension.
articles.abstract: Audio large language models (audio LLMs) process continuous speech directly and transform it into progressively more abstract representations, providing a useful computational point of comparison with human spoken-language comprehension. Previous studies have reported model-brain correspondence for pretrained speech models and text-based language models, but it remains unclear which internal representations of audio LLMs are most closely associated with neural responses during online listening. We compared EEG responses from 41 native Mandarin listeners with internal representations from Qwen2-Audio, Qwen2.5-Omni, and Kimi-Audio in a Mandarin auditory semantic-violation paradigm that controlled sentence structure and event boundaries. We extracted speech-related and word-level semantic-update representations and quantified their incremental contributions to held-out EEG prediction beyond lower-level controls. Audio LLM representations improved EEG prediction beyond the acoustic envelope, phoneme onsets, and word onsets (Δr = 0.012, corrected P = 0.028). Prediction-score partitioning indicated that semantic violation primarily increased the overlap in EEG-predictive information between speech-related and semantic-update representations, rather than the unique contribution of either representation class. This pattern was relatively stable in Qwen2-Audio and Qwen2.5-Omni and directionally consistent, although statistically weaker, in Kimi-Audio. These findings provide component-level evidence that audio-conditioned model representations correspond to human neural responses during spoken-language comprehension, without implying mechanistic equivalence.

articles.title: Age-related reversal in the behavioral relevance of theta-alpha coupling during conflict processing.
articles.abstract: Cognitive aging is often characterized by slower responses during conflict processing, but the oscillatory coordination underlying this change remains poorly understood. We examined whether cross-frequency phase synchronization between theta and alpha activity is related to response conflict processing and whether its behavioral relevance changes across adulthood. N = 117 healthy adults aged 32-84 years performed a flanker task while an EEG was recorded. Theta-alpha phase-phase coupling was quantified as phase-locking value (PLV) across task-relevant time windows; time-frequency and source-level analyses characterized the underlying dynamics. Incongruent trials produced robust behavioral conflict, with lower accuracy and slower responses than congruent trials. Theta-alpha coupling showed a pronounced 1:1 structure across conditions, and was selectively stronger during incongruent trials. Time-frequency and source-level analysis provided complementary evidence of frontocentral theta engagement and alpha modulation in posterior and sensorimotor regions. Theta-alpha PLV at FCz during the target-processing window declined with age in incongruent trials, and its association with reaction time varied with age in the incongruent-trial analysis. Stronger coupling was associated with faster responses at younger ages, whereas the same coupling was associated with slower responses at older ages. A direct comparison did not establish that this age-dependent association differed between congruent and incongruent trials. These findings suggest that theta-alpha coupling is sensitive to response conflict and may contribute to the coordination of control-related and gating-related processes. Its age-related decline and changing association with response speed highlight the relevance of cross-frequency coordination for understanding cognitive aging.

articles.title: Electroencephalography Neurophysiology Alterations in Association with Aβ and Tau Pathology Across the Symptomatic Stages of Alzheimer's Disease Continuum: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Amyloid-β (Aβ) and tau deposition drive Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, how these proteinopathies are linked to macroscopic neural activity alterations measured by electroencephalography (EEG) in symptomatic AD remains inadequately characterized. This study aims to investigate the associations between Aβ, tau, EEG neurophysiology, and cognition. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study of 73 MCI and AD participants, who underwent resting-state EEG, Aβ-PET, and tau-PET. EEG source analysis was performed to extract regional spectral power. Linear mixed-effects models were used to examine the associations of regional Aβ (quantified by SUVR), tau (binary classification), with EEG features, controlling for age, sex and education. Ordinary least squares (OLS) regression was applied to investigate the relationships of EEG spectral power and global Aβ burden with cognitive performance. RESULTS: Elevated Aβ burden was associated with distinct regional spectral alterations. Specifically, higher Aβ SUVR was significantly correlated with increased theta power and decreased beta power in a subset of cortical regions. Tau positivity did not modulate the amyloid-theta association in any region, but attenuated the amyloid-beta association in a small set of parietal regions. CONCLUSIONS: We identified a localized pattern of Aβ-related neurophysiological dysfunction across the symptomatic stages of AD continuum, characterized by theta increases and beta decreases, supporting a robust association between Aβ burden and cortical neural slowing. The findings highlight the value of source-localized EEG power as a sensitive indicator of Aβ-associated network dysfunction in AD and underscore the potential of source-localized EEG as a complementary, non-invasive biomarker for assessing pathological burden and informing diagnostic strategies in AD.

articles.title: Prognostic value of lymph node ratio beyond extranodal extension in node-positive oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Extranodal extension (ENE) is a key determinant of adjuvant therapy in node-positive oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OCSCC). However, conventional nodal staging may not fully capture the quantitative burden of nodal disease. We evaluated whether lymph node ratio (LNR) provides additional prognostic value beyond ENE in a large randomized trial cohort. METHODS AND MATERIALS: We performed a retrospective subgroup analysis of 661 node-positive patients from the phase III randomized Oral Cavity Adjuvant Therapy (OCAT) trial. LNR was defined as the metastatic-to-dissected lymph node ratio and categorized as low (<0.10) or high (≥0.10). Overall survival (OS), recurrence-free survival (RFS), and locoregional control (LRC) were estimated using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression, adjusting for ENE, T stage, N stage, PNI, margin status, LVI, and treatment arm. RESULTS: With a median follow-up of 91 months, 387 deaths occurred. On multivariable analysis, high LNR remained independently associated with inferior OS (HR 1.43, 95% CI 1.15-1.78; p = 0.001), RFS (HR 1.48; p = 0.001), and LRC (HR 1.40; p = 0.018). High LNR/ENE-positive patients had significantly worse survival than the reference group, low LNR/ENE-negative (HR 2.08, 95% CI 1.47-2.95; p < 0.001). Low LNR/ENE-positive patients trended toward inferior survival (HR 1.36; p = 0.051), while high LNR/ENE-negative patients showed no significant difference (HR 1.12; p = 0.65). CONCLUSIONS: LNR is an independent prognostic factor beyond ENE across OS, RFS, and LRC in node-positive OCSCC. High LNR combined with ENE identifies a distinctly high-risk subgroup, whereas high LNR alone did not significantly impact survival in the absence of ENE. Incorporating LNR into postoperative risk stratification may refine identification of patients for risk-adapted adjuvant strategies.

articles.title: Comparative performance of three large language models and expert radiologists in ACR TI-RADS classification of structured thyroid ultrasound reports: a retrospective analysis using cytology as reference.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly explored for medical applications. This study evaluates the agreement of three LLMs-ChatGPT, Copilot, and Gemini-with two expert radiologists in assigning ACR TI-RADS categories to thyroid nodules, using fine-needle aspiration cytology as the reference standard. METHODS: A retrospective analysis included 135 thyroid nodules from 135 unique patients (108 benign, 27 malignant). Structured TI-RADS feature scores and final categories (TR1-TR5) were extracted from existing reports generated by each LLM and two board-certified radiologists (≥8 years' experience). Agreement was assessed using Cohen's κ (feature-level), quadratic weighted κ (category-level), and diagnostic performance (sensitivity, specificity, area under the ROC curve [AUC]) with TR4-TR5 classified as test-positive categories for the binary diagnostic analysis. McNemar's test evaluated discordant classification patterns. RESULTS: Feature-level agreement was fair to substantial for composition and margin (κ up to 0.621) but poor for echogenic foci (κ as low as 0.075). Weighted κ for TI RADS categories was moderate to substantial for ChatGPT (κw 0.614-0.621) and Gemini (0.516-0.621), but fair for Copilot (0.383-0.314). All LLMs showed high sensitivity (81.5-96.3 %) but low specificity (20.4-38.0 %). Ordinal AUC values were 0.757 (ChatGPT), 0.644 (Copilot), and 0.619 (Gemini). McNemar's test suggested a more balanced discordant pattern for ChatGPT than for Copilot and Gemini. CONCLUSION: ChatGPT, Copilot, and Gemini show moderate composition/margin agreement but poor echogenic foci detection and overclassify benign nodules; standalone use is not recommended. Domain‑specific fine‑tuning and prospective validation are required.

articles.title: Impact of reader expertise on PI-RADS assessment of prostate transition zone lesions: Diagnostic performance, inter-reader agreement, and resource implications.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: PI-RADS scoring of transition zone (TZ) lesions is strongly reader-dependent, particularly in the PI-RADS 4 category. We compared diagnostic performance and inter-reader agreement between a specialized high-volume center and non-specialized referring centers. METHODS: Overall, 315 men with a TZ lesion scored PI-RADS ≥ 3 underwent MRI-guided in-bore biopsy and were stratified by interpreting site (non-specialized vs specialized). The erased-margins criterion was reassessed centrally by one specialized-center reader (the biopsy operator) and, in a 125-lesion subset, by three independent readers. RESULTS: Positive predictive value for clinically significant cancer (csPCa, Grade Group ≥ 2) at PI-RADS ≥ 4 was higher in the specialized cohort (43.3% vs 29.5%, p = 0.015). For PI-RADS 4 lesions, detection of any cancer was 76.9% vs 42.6% (p < 0.001), but not significantly different for csPCa (32.1% vs 22.8%, p = 0.16). On central reassessment, non-specialized centers had more often assigned PI-RADS 4 to lesions without erased margins (50% vs 35%, p = 0.048), a difference not replicated by the three independent readers. Agreement on PI-RADS category was substantial within and moderate between centers (κ 0.68 vs 0.43-0.49); agreement on the erased-margins criterion was fair-to-moderate (Fleiss κ 0.30), and its discriminative value decreased with decreasing expertise (AUC 0.82, 0.75, 0.70), largely reflecting lesion identification. The central reassessment did not outperform blinded readers (AUC 0.69). CONCLUSION: Specialized interpretation was associated with higher diagnostic yield for TZ lesions, particularly PI-RADS 4. Reader-dependent application of the erased-margins criterion is a candidate mechanism requiring confirmation and a potential training target rather than a stand-alone rule; prospective external validation is needed.

articles.title: Phantom-Based Evaluation of a Novel Tomographic Ultra-Fast Molecular Breast Imaging Prototype.
articles.abstract: A novel stationary tomographic Ultra-Fast Molecular Breast Imaging (UFMBI) technology was developed to reduce acquisition time and radiation dose of Molecular Breast Imaging (MBI), enabling its wider acceptance for supplemental dense breast screening. The system combines a stationary dual-head gamma camera made of CZT detectors with densely packed multi-pinhole collimators and novel de-multiplexing reconstruction methods, exploiting the ultra-high 3D position resolution of CZT detectors and their excellent energy resolution. A small field-of-view prototype (132 mm × 88 mm) was designed, built and calibrated. Raw detector data were processed using a machine-learning model providing 10×10 subpixelisation of 2 mm pixels in 5 mm thick CZT detectors and depth-of-interaction (DOI) estimation from anode signals alone. Tomographic images were reconstructed using an OSEM algorithm, including de-multiplexing and corrections for attenuation and collimator response. The prototype was evaluated using a 99mTc-filled phantom with lesions of different sizes and uniform background acquired separately. Prototype performance was compared with a clinical planar MBI system by imaging 99mTc-infused gel phantoms, with lesion detectability assessed via contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR). The results from the spheres' phantom indicated that 5-7 mm diameter lesions with tumour-to-background ratios of 10-20:1 were detectable even with a dose/time reduction factor (DRF) of 8 relative to current MBI clinical practice. The gel phantom experiments showed that, with equal activity concentration and scanning time (DRF=1), the UFMBI prototype provided 2.5 to 3.9-fold CNR of the clinical planar system depending on the lesion activity and position within the field-of-view; with DRF of 6, UFMBI provided 1.6 to 2.4-fold CNR of the clinical system, improving to 2.5 to 3.4-fold with application of non-local means noise filtering. These results demonstrate the feasibility of UFMBI as a low-dose, high throughput approach and support its further development toward cancer screening of dense breasts and image-guided biopsy applications.

articles.title: Dynamic Range Modulation via Integrated Universal Range Shifter and Ridge Filter: Enabling Simplified Delivery for FLASH-Enabled IMPT.
articles.abstract: In proton FLASH therapy, using a transmission beam with hypofractionated doses can minimize energy layer switching interruptions to preserve FLASH effect. However, intensity-modulated proton therapy (IMPT) struggles to achieve high FLASH dose rates. This study proposes a novel system that combines universal range shifters (URS) and universal ridge filters (URF) to enable FLASH effect in IMPT.Approach: Water equivalent thickness (WET) optimization was first performed to determine the URS thickness relative to tumor depth, followed by URF modulation to broaden the monoenergetic Bragg peak for longitudinal target coverage. Plan optimization incorporated a spot sparsification algorithm. The proposed system using 218 MeV beams was evaluated in three anatomical sites (brain, liver, and lung tumors) for 10 cases each. Furthermore, this study evaluated the impact of hardware switching speeds and two delivery strategies: (1) bi-URS, constraining URS transitions to binary states, and (2) bi-URF, restricting URF modulation to binary configurations.Main Results: The bi-URS and TB plans achieved mean D98% of 98.30% ± 0.80% versus 98.60% ± 0.90% in brain cases, and 98.40% ± 0.50% versus 97.20% ± 1.00% in liver cases, respectively. Compared to bi-URF, the bi-URS modality significantly reduced delivery time (e.g., brain: 0.305 ± 0.09 s vs. 1.031 ± 0.096 s, p < 0.001). And it demonstrated superior target conformity index (CI) (brain: 0.660 ± 0.020 and liver: 0.653 ± 0.022) compared to TB plans (brain: 0.357 ± 0.082, p < 0.001 and liver: 0.479 ± 0.100, p = 0.012) while maintaining high FLASH average dose rate (ADR) coverage (V40Gy/s of 87.60 ± 15.96% for brain and 91.21 ± 14.42% for liver cases) with URF 20-ms switching speed. Furthermore, it effectively spared the Dmax of hippocampus (bi-URS: 19.00 ± 5.80 Gy, TB: 37.71 ± 17.71 Gy, p=0.041) in brain cases and the residual liver V5 Gy in liver cases (bi-URS: 27.79 ± 10.9%, TB: 68.64 ± 18.72% , p=0.002). However, in lung cases, the CI of the bi-URS modality, while superior to that of the TB modality, remained below the clinical expectation of 0.6.Significance: The combined URS and URF delivery strategy (bi-URS) improved dose conformity of the target, and maintained high FLASH effect coverage in brain and liver cases, demonstrating its potential as a Bragg-peak PBS approach for FLASH radiotherapy.&#xD.

articles.title: Early-phase single-time-point kidney dosimetry in 177Lu-DOTATATE therapy using a half-life fraction-based correction: a retrospective single-center evaluation.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Multi-time-point kidney dosimetry for 177Lu-DOTATATE peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) is resource-intensive, and delayed-phase imaging is infeasible where PRRT is delivered during a short hospitalization. We evaluated a single-time-point (STP) method using a cohort-specific half-life fraction (HLF) correction at 4-120 h post-injection. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 17 patients (34 kidneys) after a first 177Lu-DOTATATE cycle (October 2021-January 2024). Reference doses came from a 4-time-point (4TP) SPECT/CT protocol at 4, 24, 72 and 120 h. STP doses were compared with the reference by mean percent error (MPE), root mean square error (RMSE), Bland-Altman analysis and the Friedman test with Holm post-hoc correction. Four-fold cross-validation, with the HLF re-derived from training folds only, was applied at 4 and 24 h. RESULTS: The mean 4TP dose was 3120.5 ± 1015.7 mGy. STP (4 h) gave 3307.6 ± 1131.7 mGy (not significantly different), whereas 24, 72 and 120 h significantly overestimated it. The whole-cohort MPE was 8.3 ± 31.1% for STP (4 h) and 27.9 ± 26.0% for STP (24 h). The Bland-Altman bias of STP (4 h) (4TP - STP, -187 mGy) did not differ from zero, whereas that of STP (24 h) (-​​818 mGy) did. Cross-validated errors (MPE 17.1 ± 14.6% at 4 h, 9.3 ± 8.8% at 24 h) may have been affec​ted by differences involumes of interest (VOIs) ​between analyses and did not establish the superiority of either time point. CONCLUSION: HLF-corrected STP dosimetry is feasible during short-stay PRRT for toxicity-oriented renal dose estimation. STP (4 h) showed no systematic bias against the reference. STP (24 h) systematically overestimated it but fits routine radiation-safety and scheduling constraints. Both findings require confirmation in independent cohorts. Neither approach replaces multi-time-point dosimetry.

articles.title: Associations of plasma biomarkers and amyloid positron emission tomography with regional tau burden in Alzheimer's disease.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) and plasma biomarkers are clinically established; however, their topographical relationship with regional tau burden remains unclear. We investigated whether amyloid PET and plasma biomarkers are associated with regional tau pathology, measured using second-generation tracer florzolotau (18F) PET, across the Alzheimer's disease (AD) continuum. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional study enrolled participants who underwent biomarker assessment between September 2018 and May 2022. The primary outcome was the voxel-wise spatial correlation of florzolotau (18F) standardised uptake value ratio with amyloid PET centiloid and plasma biomarkers, assessed using age- and sex-adjusted whole-brain and region-of-interest (ROI) linear regression analyses, including multivariate models adjusted for amyloid PET centiloid. RESULTS: The study included 92 individuals (mean age, 71 [standard deviation, 8.8] years; 46 men), comprising 40 amyloid-negative healthy controls, 10 patients with preclinical AD, 21 with mild cognitive impairment due to AD, and 21 with AD dementia. In initial analyses, regional tau uptake correlated widely with plasma amyloid-beta 42/40 (Aβ42/40) ratio, p-tau, and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP). However, following multivariate adjustment for global amyloid burden, correlations for Aβ42/40 and GFAP were completely abolished. In contrast, plasma p-tau217, p-tau181, and neurofilament light chain (NfL) maintained significant amyloid-independent correlations with temporoparietal tau uptake, with p-tau217 uniquely retaining robust and extensive associations across the cortex. CONCLUSION: Plasma p-tau217 is strongly associated with the spatial distribution and severity of tau burden independent of global amyloid burden. Measuring plasma p-tau217 holds significant potential for patient stratification and monitoring in the era of disease-modifying therapies. TRIAL REGISTRATION: UMIN Clinical Trials Registry (UMIN000032027), registered 31 March 2018, prospectively registered (URL https//center6.umin.ac.jp/cgiopenbin/ctr_e/ctr_view.cgi? recptno=UMIN000032027). Japan Registry of Clinical Trials (jRCTs031180225), prospectively registered (URL https//jrct.niph.go.jp/enlatestdetail/jRCTs031180225).

articles.title: Serial quantitative CT volume change in fibrotic interstitial lung disease: associations with mortality, acute exacerbation, and pulmonary function decline.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate whether serial quantitative computed tomography (CT) volume change is associated with mortality, acute exacerbation, and concurrent pulmonary function decline in fibrotic interstitial lung disease. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 102 participants who underwent surgical lung biopsy and paired CT between October 2018 and August 2023. A deep learning-based quantitative CT system measured fibrotic lesion and normal-lung volumes. Spearman correlations compared CT measures. Cox models assessed baseline volumes and annualized changes; linear models assessed concurrent pulmonary function change. RESULTS: Median age was 65 years [interquartile range, 56-69]; 68 participants were men. During median 4.82 years of follow-up, 12 deaths and 15 acute exacerbations occurred. Fibrotic lesion and normal-lung volumes were inversely correlated at baseline and follow-up, as were their annualized changes (ρ = -0.53, - 0.60, and - 0.56, respectively). Annualized fibrotic lesion volume increase (hazard ratio per 100 mL/year, 1.40; 95% confidence interval 1.15-1.69; q = 0.0036) and annualized normal-lung volume loss (hazard ratio per 500 mL/year decrease, 1.57; 95% confidence interval 1.20-2.06; q = 0.0036) were associated with death. Baseline fibrotic lesion volume was associated with acute exacerbation (hazard ratio per 100 mL, 1.33; 95% confidence interval 1.09-1.63; q = 0.012). Greater fibrotic lesion increase and normal-lung loss were associated with forced vital capacity decline; diffusing capacity associations were not significant after correction. CONCLUSION: Serial quantitative CT volume change was associated with mortality and concurrent forced vital capacity decline, whereas baseline fibrotic lesion burden was associated with acute exacerbation in fibrotic interstitial lung disease.

articles.title: Cortical morphometric similarity alterations and molecular correlates in acute ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Ischemic stroke is associated with distributed cortical structural alterations, but the molecular context of acute-stage morphometric similarity (MS) changes remains unclear. This study aimed to characterize MS alterations in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) and examine their spatial transcriptomic correlates using the Allen Human Brain Atlas. METHODS: In this cross-sectional case-control study, 36 patients with first-ever AIS involving the unilateral basal ganglia and/or corona radiata and 36 healthy controls (HCs) were included. Patients were enrolled within 7 days after symptom onset, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was performed in the acute stage. Whole-brain MS networks were derived from multiple cortical morphometric features. Group differences in regional MS were assessed with adjustment for age, sex, education, and infarction volume. Spatial associations between MS alterations and gene expression were examined using partial least squares regression with post-mortem transcriptomic data from the Allen Human Brain Atlas (AHBA). Correlations between regional MS values and plasma metal concentrations were examined in patients with AIS. RESULTS: AIS patients exhibited regionally heterogeneous MS alterations, with increased MS mainly in the lateral occipital, lingual, postcentral, and pericalcarine cortices, and decreased MS mainly in the superior frontal, precuneus, and superior temporal regions. Imaging-transcriptomic integration showed that these spatial MS changes were associated with gene expression profiles related to neuronal viability, transcriptional co-regulation, and cellular stress-related pathways. After permutation testing and false discovery rate (FDR) correction, significant associations were identified between right precuneus MS and plasma lead (Pb) and cesium (Cs) levels. CONCLUSIONS: These findings identify region-specific MS alterations in AIS and provide spatial transcriptomic context for early post-stroke structural changes.

articles.title: Susceptibility-weighted imaging findings in subacute sclerosing panencephalitis: subcortical paramagnetic rim and deep gray matter changes.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder caused by persistent measles virus infection. Conventional MRI plays a key role in diagnosis and staging; however, susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) findings in SSPE have not been systematically characterized, particularly with respect to their relationship to disease burden and neurodegeneration. With this study we aim to evaluate SWI changes in SSPE, with emphasis on the Subcortical Paramagnetic Rim (SPR) and deep gray matter mineralization, and to assess their association with parenchymal disease burden and cerebral atrophy. METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 126 patients with confirmed SSPE who underwent MRI including SWI. T2/FLAIR hyperintensities were assessed across predefined supratentorial and infratentorial parenchymal regions. A composite total parenchymal disease burden score was calculated. Cerebral atrophy and deep gray matter mineralization were evaluated using semi-quantitative visual grading systems. SWI was also assessed for the presence of a SPR. Associations between susceptibility findings, parenchymal disease burden, cerebral atrophy, and clinical parameters were analyzed using non-parametric statistical methods. RESULTS: SPR was identified in 14 of 128 MRI studies (10.9%), most commonly involving the parietal lobes. Patients with the rim had significantly longer symptom duration, higher disease stage, greater parenchymal disease burden, higher atrophy scores, and higher deep gray matter mineralization scores compared with patients without the rim (p < 0.01). Deep gray matter mineralization scores showed significant positive correlations with both global parenchymal disease burden and cerebral atrophy (Spearman's ρ, p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: SPR and deep gray matter mineralization, are associated with increasing parenchymal disease burden and atrophy. These findings likely represent imaging markers of disease chronicity and provide complementary information to conventional MRI, particularly in the evaluation of chronic encephalitis in measles-endemic regions.

articles.title: Calcification below the anterior arch of the atlas: avoiding misdiagnosis as acute calcific tendinitis of the longus colli.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To assess the CT features of incidental calcification below the anterior arch of the atlas (ICBAAA) and compare them with acute calcific tendinitis of the longus colli muscle (ACTLCM). METHODS: This retrospective study included 500 patients without acute neck pain who underwent sinonasal CT including the craniocervical junction and extending through the inferior margin of C2, and 11 patients with ACTLCM. Calcifications/ossifications below the anterior arch of the atlas were assessed qualitatively and quantitatively by two radiologists and compared between groups. RESULTS: ICBAAA was identified in 149 of 500 patients (29.8%). Patients with ICBAAA were older than those with ACTLCM (median age, 69 vs. 43 years, p < 0.001). Cortical attenuation (84% vs. 18%) and atlantoaxial osteoarthritis (66% vs. 0%) were more frequent in ICBAAA than in ACTLCM (both p < 0.001). In contrast, multiplicity (19% vs. 100%, p < 0.001), paramedian distribution (27% vs. 100%, p < 0.001), asymmetry (26% vs. 100%, p < 0.001), ill-defined margins (14% vs. 91%, p < 0.001), and irregular borders (27% vs. 73%, p = 0.003) were more frequent in ACTLCM than in ICBAAA. Median CT attenuation values were higher in ICBAAA than in ACTLCM (1063 vs. 566 HU), whereas the median number (1 vs. 4) and maximum diameter (3 vs. 10 mm) of calcifications were greater in ACTLCM than in ICBAAA (all p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: ICBAAA was common in this selected sinonasal CT cohort and showed imaging differences from ACTLCM. These exploratory findings require validation in larger, protocol-matched cohorts.

articles.title: Evaluation of articular cartilage of the glenohumeral joint in patients with labral tears using T2 mapping technique on MRI: Is there a correlation between cartilage T2 values and labral tear location or frequency of shoulder dislocation?
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to evaluate glenohumeral cartilage using T2 mapping and to investigate whether cartilage T2 values were associated with labral tear location and frequency of shoulder dislocation. METHODS: In this prospective study, 30 shoulder MRIs with T2 mapping were performed at a 3.0 T scanner. T2 values of cartilage were measured twice by two radiologists after dividing the glenoid and humeral side into 9 areas as: anterosuperior, anterior_middle, anteroinferior, central_superior, central_middle, central_inferior, posterosuperior, posterior_middle, posteroinferior. Intra- and interobserver agreements were calculated using intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Labral tears were classified according to location into following groups: superior labral tear group (10-2 o'clock), anterior labral tear group (2-6 o'clock), posterior labral tear group (6-10 o'clock), inferior labral tear group (5-7 o'clock), MDI group (multidirectional instability, involving 3 quadrants or more). Correlations were analyzed using independent student T and ANOVA tests. RESULTS: Overall interobserver agreement was moderate (glenoid, 0.612; humeral head, 0.530), whereas intraobserver agreement was good (glenoid, 0.763; humeral head, 0.866). Glenoid cartilage T2 values differed significantly between tear-location groups in the anterosuperior and posteroinferior regions. Cartilage T2 values were not significantly associated with the frequency of shoulder dislocation. CONCLUSION: Interobserver agreement was moderate overall but varied by region, whereas intraobserver agreement was good. Labral tear location was associated with significant differences in T2 values in the anterosuperior and posteroinferior glenoid cartilage regions. No significant association was observed between cartilage T2 values and the frequency of shoulder dislocation.

articles.title: Highlights of the Annual Scientific Meeting of the Australasian Musculoskeletal Imaging Group (AMSIG) 2026, Sydney, Australia.
Role of Pancreatic Shear Wave Elastography in Children with Type 1 Diabetes: A Comparative and Correlative Study with Clinical and Laboratory Parameters.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate pancreatic stiffness in children with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) using two-dimensional shear wave elastography (2D-SWE), compare findings with age‑matched controls, and assess associations with pancreatic size, clinical parameters, and disease duration. METHODS: Seventy‑six children (38 T1DM, 38 controls) aged 5-18 years underwent standardized pancreatic ultrasound with SWE of the head, body, and tail. Three readings per region were averaged. Pancreatic dimensions, fasting blood sugar (FBS), HbA1c, and clinical details were recorded. Group comparisons and correlation analyses were performed. RESULTS: Children with T1DM showed significantly higher stiffness than controls across all regions (p < 0.001). Mean SWE increased with disease duration: recent‑onset 3.11 ± 1.02 kPa, intermediate 4.72 ± 0.88 kPa, long‑standing 6.29 ± 0.81 kPa; controls 2.85 ± 0.31 kPa. Pancreatic size was smaller in diabetics, with progressive reduction correlating with chronicity. SWE showed a strong positive correlation with disease duration (ρ = 0.823, p < 0.001) and an inverse correlation with pancreatic size. No meaningful association was seen between SWE and HbA1c or FBS. ROC analysis demonstrated good discriminatory performance of pancreatic SWE for differentiating children with T1DM from healthy controls. CONCLUSIONS: Pancreatic stiffness is increased in children with T1DM and rises progressively with disease duration while pancreatic size declines. SWE reflects long‑term structural change rather than short‑term glycaemic status. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This study demonstrates that pancreatic SWE provides quantitative measures of pancreatic stiffness and helps elucidate its associations with pancreatic size and disease duration in children with T1DM.

articles.title: Adaptive Mask-Guided k-Space Diffusion for Accelerated MRI Reconstruction.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Masked modeling has emerged as a powerful deep learning paradigm that reconstructs missing data by predicting masked regions, achieving strong performance across multiple domains. As a critical task in medical imaging, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) reconstruction aims to recover high-quality images from under-sampled k-space data. However, existing methods usually optimize the full image domain or k-space, while overlooking the importance and structural roles of different frequency components. METHODS: An adaptive mask-guided diffusion model (AMDM) was developed, which leverages adaptively estimated frequency distributions from k-space to construct a hybrid mask mechanism for handling diverse k-space inputs. It enables the effective separation of high-frequency and low-frequency components, producing multiple prior representations. In addition, the frequency distribution is used to generate adaptive masks, which subsequently guide the closed-loop diffusion process. RESULTS: Experimental results demonstrated improved reconstruction performance through frequency-aware modeling. AMDM achieved a PSNR of 36.89 dB on an independent public brain dataset without retraining, even at an under-sampling factor of R = 12  . CONCLUSION: The proposed method shows that explicitly modeling k-space frequency heterogeneity provides an effective prior for MRI reconstruction, offering a promising direction for robust reconstruction under aggressive under-sampling.

articles.title: Short T1 Fraction as a Marker of Myelin Content: Evidence From Postmortem MRI and Histology.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate the short-T1 fraction as a potential biomarker of white matter myelin integrity, using myelin histology as ground truth. METHODS: Multi-inversion-time MRI data were acquired from four postmortem brain specimens from donors with Alzheimer's disease on a clinical 3T scanner, and from five dissected tissue blocks containing white matter hyperintensities (WMHs) on a preclinical 3T system. Short-T1 fraction maps were generated using inverse Laplace transform to isolate short-T1 components and were compared with T2-based myelin water imaging metrics through joint T1-T2 correlation analysis. Short-T1 fraction maps from the tissue blocks were further compared with myelin histology. In addition, in vivo short-T1 fraction data were acquired from five participants, including four healthy male volunteers (35.4 ± 12.1 years) and one 71-year-old female participant with moderate white matter microangiopathy and WMHs, to demonstrate translational feasibility. RESULTS: Postmortem MRI revealed reduced short-T1 fractions in WMHs. T1-T2 correlation analysis suggested that the short-T1 fraction was closely associated with the short-T2 (myelin water) component. Strong correlations were observed between short-T1 fractions and optical densities from both Luxol Fast Blue- and Myelin Basic Protein-stained histological sections, supporting the link between the short-T1 signal and myelin content. Preliminary in vivo findings also showed reduced short-T1 fraction within WMHs, consistent with the ex vivo observations. CONCLUSION: The short-T1 fraction correlated with myelin content in postmortem brain white matter, supporting its potential as a biomarker of myelin integrity.

articles.title: Stim-CODE: PNS and CNS Constraint Optimized Diffusion-Encoding for Neuroimaging on 200 mT/m Whole-Body Gradients.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Ultra-high-performance whole-body MRI gradients (  G max   ≥  200mT/m,  S max   ≥  200 T/m/s) can reduce echo times (TE) in diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), improving SNR. However, full hardware utilization is limited by cardiac (CNS) and peripheral (PNS) nerve stimulation thresholds. This work demonstrates Stimulation Constraint Optimized diffusion-encoding (Stim-CODE) for neuro diffusion. METHODS: Stim-CODE uses the gradient optimization (GrOpt) toolbox to optimally design diffusion-encoding gradient waveforms subject to a CNS or PNS "constraint envelope" based on other gradient events in the sequence. Stim-CODE was evaluated in simulations and in vivo protocols with in-plane resolutions of 1.5 ×  1.5 mm   2   and 1.0 ×  1.0 mm   2   across G   max   = [45, 80, 200] mT/m and  S max = 200  T/m/s. Healthy volunteers (N = 10) underwent neuro DWI at b = 1000 s/mm   2   with Monopolar, Stim-CODE-  M 0   , Bipolar, and Stim-CODE-  M 1   encoding. SNR, apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) maps, and ADC uncertainty were quantified. One volunteer underwent DTI with the same encoding schemes acquired at b  = [1000, 3000]s/mm   2   . RESULTS: Stim-CODE reduced TEs across all b  -values, with larger gains for higher resolutions, greater G   max   , and  M 1   -nulled waveforms. Phantom and in vivo experiments confirmed equivalent diffusion-weighting with TE savings and SNR improvements. Stim-CODE-  M 1   had significant SNR gains over Bipolar scans, but some differences in global ADC were observed. DTI metrics were similar across scans, with Stim-CODE showing lower uncertainty. CONCLUSION: Stim-CODE maximizes hardware capabilities to achieve time-optimized diffusion-encoding while respecting CNS and PNS, enabling similar diffusion-weighting as conventional approaches with reduced TE and higher SNR.

articles.title: Quantitative Proton Density Mapping With Data-Driven Reception Profile Correction Derived From Macromolecular Proton Fraction.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Proton density (PD) and macromolecular proton fraction (MPF) are fundamental MR parameters characterizing water and macromolecular content in tissues. Both parameters can be mapped using a time-efficient MRI protocol, though PD maps require additional corrections for the reception profile (RP) non-uniformity and global scaling. Existing PD mapping methods suffer from uncertainties related to PD normalization to reference tissue. This study aimed to develop a data-driven RP correction method for PD mapping based on MPF as an internal scale. THEORY AND METHODS: One-parameter model linking PD and MPF was derived under the assumption of proportionality between total macromolecular volume and proton concentration. This model, with a uniform parameter value across brain tissues, generates a surrogate PD map, which is used to estimate RP from an uncorrected PD map. The proposed algorithm was tested against a common PD mapping method utilizing bias-field correction and normalization to cerebrospinal fluid. Brain MRI data were acquired at 3 T from seven healthy individuals. The protocol included 3D multi-echo T1-, PD-, and magnetization-transfer-weighted gradient-echo sequences. Parametric maps were reconstructed using the single-point MPF mapping algorithm with data-driven B1 correction. RESULTS: MPF-based and bias-field corrections yielded similar PD measurements in white and gray matter with no significant bias and remarkably small variability (coefficients of variation < 0.6%). CONCLUSIONS: MPF-based RP correction enables computationally simple and robust quantitative PD mapping at no additional cost if MPF maps are available. The main advantage of the proposed method is the automatic elimination of global scaling that obviates the need for PD normalization.

articles.title: Time-Resolved 3D Imaging and Strain Analysis of the Skeletal Muscle.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To develop and validate a method for time-resolved 3D imaging and strain analysis that enables quantification of dynamic in vivo muscle deformations from aperiodic continuous motion. THEORY AND METHODS: Controlled deformations were induced in the thigh muscles of eight healthy volunteers using a pneumatic pressure cuff, both under passive conditions and during isometric muscle contractions. An iterative reconstruction approach based on the Spectro-Dynamic MRI framework was formulated for joint reconstruction of time-resolved 3D images and velocity fields from highly undersampled k-space data at 1.4 Hz. The accuracy of the results was evaluated against fully sampled images, acquired under static conditions with similar deformations. Octahedral shear strain (OSS) values were computed from the estimated motion fields. Mean OSS values were calculated for all thigh muscles, and differences in the mean OSS values between passive and isometric contraction conditions were assessed. RESULTS: The reconstructed time-resolved images closely matched the fully sampled validation images and the estimated motion fields accurately captured the deformations. Isometric muscle contraction resulted in reduced displacements and lower mean OSS values compared with the passive condition. The largest reduction in mean OSS value was consistently observed in the hamstring muscles, which become stiffer during isometric knee flexion. CONCLUSION: Our proposed reconstruction approach enables robust time-resolved 3D strain estimates in muscles using data from a single motion repetition. This method provides new opportunities for investigating the temporal evolution of in vivo displacements and strains in a dynamic setting.
